exposure: Ultrasound guided QL Block with 0.25% ropivacaine
Ultrasound guided TAP Block with 0.25% ropivacaine
cohort: Sixty patients undergoing elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia were randomly divided into two equal groups for different nerve blocks.
finding: Ultrasound guided Quadratus Lumborum (QL) Block demonstrated superior analgesic efficacy compared to Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) Block, providing prolonged analgesia, lower VAS scores, reduced opioid consumption, and extended time for first rescue analgesia in the postoperative period after cesarean section.
